runbooks.title: Payment Service Outage Runbook
runbooks.description: Step-by-step guide for handling payment service outages in production

steps.title: Acknowledge and triage
actions: Acknowledge PagerDuty alert within 5 minutes
Join #incident-response Slack channel
Check CloudWatch dashboard: https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch/payment-service
Identify error rate, latency p99, and affected endpoints
Set incident severity in Jira (P1 if error rate > 50%, P2 if > 10%)

steps.title: Identify root cause
actions: Check recent deployments in deployment-history dashboard (last 2 hours)
Review CloudWatch logs for ERROR messages: `aws logs filter-log-events --log-group /aws/payment-service/application --filter-pattern ERROR`
Check DB connection pool metrics: CloudWatch > payment-service > hikaricp.connections.active
Check postgres-primary RDS metrics: DatabaseConnections, FreeStorageSpace, CPUUtilization
Review GitHub for recent merged PRs in last 24 hours
Check if error correlates with deployment timestamp

steps.title: Immediate mitigation - DB Connection Pool Exhaustion
steps.condition: If CloudWatch shows HikariCP pool exhausted
actions: IMMEDIATE: Initiate rollback of latest deployment if deployed in last 2 hours
Run: `aws ecs update-service --cluster prod-cluster --service payment-service --force-new-deployment`
Kill long-running DB queries: `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname='payments_db' AND state='active' AND query_start < NOW() - INTERVAL '5 minutes';`
If rollback not possible, temporarily reduce pool size: update SSM parameter /prod/payment-service/HIKARI_MAX_POOL_SIZE to 20
Scale down payment-service instances to reduce total DB connections: `aws ecs update-service --desired-count 1`

steps.title: Rollback procedure
actions: Identify last stable version from deployment history
Trigger rollback pipeline: https://jenkins.company.com/payment-service-rollback
Or manually: `aws ecs update-service --cluster prod-cluster --service payment-service --task-definition payment-service:<PREVIOUS_VERSION>`
Monitor: Wait 5 minutes, verify error rate drops below 1%
Verify DB connections normalize: CloudWatch > hikaricp.connections.active < 20

steps.title: Verify recovery
actions: Error rate < 0.5%
p99 latency < 500ms
DB connections < 30 (back to normal pool size)
No new ERROR log entries in last 2 minutes
Send all-clear to #incident-response

steps.title: Post-incident
actions: Update Jira ticket with timeline and resolution
Schedule post-mortem within 48 hours
Create follow-up tickets for permanent fix
Update this runbook if steps were insufficient

steps.title: Check current connections
actions: Connect to RDS: `psql -h postgres-primary.cluster-xxx.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com -U admin -d payments_db`
Run: `SELECT count(*), state, datname FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY state, datname ORDER BY count DESC;`
Identify which service is consuming most connections

steps.title: Kill idle/blocked connections
actions: Kill idle connections older than 10 minutes: `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'idle' AND query_start < NOW() - INTERVAL '10 minutes';`
Kill blocked connections: `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE wait_event_type = 'Lock' AND query_start < NOW() - INTERVAL '1 minute';`

steps.title: Temporary connection limit increase
actions: Modify RDS parameter group: `aws rds modify-db-parameter-group --db-parameter-group-name prod-pg15 --parameters ParameterName=max_connections,ParameterValue=200,ApplyMethod=pending-reboot`
Note: Requires DB restart for non-dynamic parameters. Coordinate with team.
